summary: sitecard: publicly-tunneled SSH-to-shell gateway with optional no-auth mode
details: sitecard is a CLI whose advertised and documented function is to spawn a local AsyncSSH server on 127.0.0.1:4822 and expose it to the public internet via a reverse tunnel (default srv.us/*.srv.us, with Cloudflare Worker relay and upterm as alternatives). Incoming SSH sessions are allocated a PTY and their bytes are piped directly into a child shell process (gateway.py `pump_ssh_input` forwards client bytes to `child.stdin.write`), giving whoever reaches the tunnel URL an interactive shell on the host. Authentication is by password plus authorized_keys by default, but a `--public-access` flag (alias `--accept`) causes `TokenSSHServer.begin_auth` to return False, disabling authentication entirely so any party that reaches the public tunnel URL can execute commands. The channel only comes up when the user explicitly runs `sitecard start`; there are no install-time or import-time lifecycle hooks, no credential harvesting, no filesystem persistence beyond the running process, and no second/undisclosed channel. The publicly-tunneled shell and the no-auth mode are described in the package's own documentation, so this is a disclosed remote-shell product rather than a covert backdoor, but the `--public-access` mode is a full unauthenticated remote code execution surface on the installer's host for the duration the CLI is running.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
